title: Repository bootstrap and canonical agent protocol
purpose: Establish the vendor-neutral repository protocol required before G0 packages can become Ready.

include: Canonical agent guide and thin Codex/Claude adapters
Machine-readable protocol schemas and directory structure
Repository consistency and synthetic-only secret-scan evidence
Approved bootstrap runtime, lockfile, Node-only protocol validator, and read-only CI workflow
exclude: Product/domain implementation, schema migrations, provider integrations, and credentials

acceptance_criteria: Canonical guide is the sole full agent-policy source and adapters only point to it.
Role profiles use stable role IDs and display names without pretending that an unassigned role is an agent run.
Package, status, handoff, and capability schemas declare protocol version 1.0.0.
The named Author, Reviewer, Tester, and Integration Owner IDs are non-empty and pairwise distinct before a package is Ready or later.
No production secret or customer data is introduced.
The package has real role assignments and may advance only through independent review, test, and integration evidence.
required_tests: JSON syntax validation for all .agents schemas and JSON manifests
Node-only role-separation validator for every Ready-or-later JSON manifest
Node-only capability-profile validator that requires declarations for every Ready-or-later role run
Node-only synthetic secret-pattern scan of repository candidate files
Pinned Node/npm version and npm clean-install verification
Synthetic-only secret-pattern scan of newly added tracked files
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert the bootstrap-only commit; no persisted data or external state is created.
open_blockers: Cross-vendor protocol dry run is required for G0 evidence and cannot be represented by a placeholder.
Repository branch protection requires an authorized repository administrator.
Product Owner approval and a real Product/UX approval assignment are required; an A5 representative dry run is not a substitute.
Capability declarations and benchmark references must map real agent runs to required skill profiles before later packages become Ready.
